title: ShiftSwap: last-minute shift cover for UK hospitality

problem_severity_frequency.rationale: ONS/UKHospitality data show acute labour pressure and unfilled roles, so uncovered shifts are plausibly frequent and painful; no venue confirmed it is the binding pain.

buyer_budget_clarity.rationale: Venue owners control a small software budget but it is anchored to £0-£49/mo commodity tools, leaving little headroom.

evidence_strength.rationale: Credible secondary ONS-derived labour-market data plus vendor pages; no primary buyer or payment evidence.

distribution.rationale: Two-sided adoption (venues and their staff); no credible non-paid route to critical mass identified.

differentiation.rationale: Every surveyed low-cost UK rota product already bundles self-service shift swaps; no wedge on top of existing tools.

validation_speed_cost.rationale: A small concierge test is cheap, but disconfirming the two-sided adoption problem requires access to both venues and staff.

feasibility.rationale: Technically straightforward; scheduling/notification tooling is well understood. Feasibility was not the blocker.

economics.rationale: Advertised alternatives at £0, £9, £10 and £49/mo leave no defensible price above acquisition cost.

founder_fit.rationale: No evidence recorded about founder domain access or distribution in hospitality; left unscored rather than guessed.

risk.rationale: Workforce data privacy is manageable; main risk is commodity competition rather than regulation.

economic_buyer.note: Venue owner/GM controls a small software budget, though anchored to £0-£49/mo commodity tools.

painful_frequent_or_budgeted.note: Uncovered shifts are frequent and operationally painful in hospitality (ONS/UKHospitality labour-market evidence).

non_paid_distribution.note: Two-sided venue+staff adoption; no credible non-paid route to critical mass on either side.

defensible_wedge.note: Every low-cost UK rota product surveyed already bundles self-service shift swaps; no wedge.

no_network_effects_needed.note: Cover value depends on enough participating staff per venue; a cross-venue marketplace adds further density requirements.

plausible_margins.note: Advertised alternatives at £0/£9/£10/£49 per month leave no viable price above cost of acquisition.

acceptable_risk.note: No material regulatory risk identified; workforce data can be handled with standard controls.

cheap_disconfirming_test.note: A 10-venue concierge cover test could be run cheaply and quickly.

not_all_optimistic.note: Viability requires simultaneous venue and staff adoption plus a low-CAC channel; every assumption must hold.
